text: just seen a guy restart the same paragraph four times in one hour. laptop open. phone face down like that does anything. no screen time limits. no airplane mode. no opal. just him and his own willpower against every notification on earth. document still called untitled. brave. genuinely stupid. but brave.
base_video: Creator sitting at a library or cafe table with an open notebook, looking off camera at someone, then doing a slow double take back to lens with raised eyebrows.
audio: quiet lofi study sound, low volume
caption: face down does nothing. who else is like this
why_this_brand: A half-written doc and a hand that keeps reaching for the phone is the desk scene Opal's focus blocking is built around, on phone and desktop.
what_changed: Dropped 'no phone in another room' so the list stays one tight beat, everything else untouched.

format.reason: Opal is an app with no physical demo moment, and its whole pull is the relatable 'old way' pile: deleting Instagram then redownloading it, airplane mode, phone in another room. A silent reacting person at 11:40pm in bed with one block of text about losing the night to 'one more video' lets the pain land in 1.5 seconds and the product arrive as the discovery, not the announcement.
format.why_not_runner_up: A carousel of old-way screenshots could work, but Opal has no strong visual before/after to swipe through and slides lose the face-plus-audio hold that drives first-post reach.

editor_fix: Trim 'no phone in another room' to just 'phone in another room? no' or drop it, the list is one beat long and the rest is already perfect.
